title: LiveEdit: Real-Time Streaming Video Editing
hook: A three-stage distillation pipeline turns a slow, bidirectional video editor into a causal, frame-by-frame one fast enough for live AR — 12.66 FPS with stable backgrounds.
key_points: Streaming video editing must hold backgrounds and untouched regions steady over time while running in real time — most editors manage only one.
A three-stage distillation pipeline transfers editing skill from a powerful bidirectional model into an efficient, causal streaming editor.
An AR-oriented mask cache reuses region-specific computation across frames instead of recomputing it every frame.
Reaches 12.66 FPS with state-of-the-art visual quality among streaming baselines, on a new dedicated benchmark.
content_html: Editing a video frame-by-frame in real time is harder than generating one from scratch: the background and untouched regions must stay rock-steady while the edit keeps pace with a live feed. LiveEdit is a streaming video editor built for exactly that trade-off.
extra_html: Most recent streaming generation methods target pure synthesis and can't be dropped into editing, which demands strict preservation of untouched content plus region-specific control. LiveEdit's key idea is a three-stage distillation pipeline that progressively transfers editing capability from a powerful bidirectional foundation model into an efficient, causal, frame-by-frame streaming editor — enabling stable long-horizon edits without sacrificing visual fidelity. An AR-oriented mask cache reuses region-related computation across frames rather than recomputing it each time, cutting redundant work. On a new dedicated streaming-editing benchmark, the method hits state-of-the-art visual quality among streaming baselines while running at 12.66 FPS — fast enough for interactive and augmented-reality use. Xinyu Wang, Chongbo Zhao, Fangneng Zhan, and Yue Ma, arXiv 2026.

related.hook: OpenAI's Sora 2 added synchronized audio and sharper physical consistency — and shipped inside a TikTok-style social app where you remix each other's generations.

related.title: Veo 3
related.hook: Google's Veo 3 generates video with synchronized native audio — dialogue, sound effects, and ambient noise produced together with the picture, not dubbed on after.

related.title: ReFreeKV: Threshold-Free KV Cache Compression
related.hook: Most KV-cache pruning needs a hand-tuned budget threshold per input — pick wrong and performance craters. ReFreeKV adapts the budget on the fly instead.

flashcards.prompt: What are the two things that make streaming video editing hard, per this paper?
flashcards.back_html: Keeping backgrounds and non-edited regions stable over time, and hitting the low latency real-time interaction demands — most methods only manage one of the two.

flashcards.prompt: How does LiveEdit turn a slow bidirectional editor into a fast streaming one?

choices.text: A three-stage distillation pipeline that progressively transfers editing ability into a causal, unidirectional model
Simply reducing the resolution of every frame
Skipping every other frame to save compute

flashcards.explanation_html: The distillation stages gradually hand off editing capability to a lighter, causal streaming model without sacrificing fidelity.

flashcards.prompt: What does the AR-oriented mask cache save on?
flashcards.back_html: It reuses region-related computation across frames instead of recomputing masks from scratch each frame, cutting redundant work and speeding inference.
